help:metadata.help:title: Ordo 1.2.6: Complete Rating, Reporting, and Workflow Help
help:metadata.help:subtitle: Rate PGN result pools, control identifiability, model uncertainty, and generate interoperable reports
help:metadata.help:abstract: Ordo reads completed game results from PGN, optionally normalizes and selects participants, checks whether the result graph is rateable, fits relative player strengths, and emits rating, uncertainty, matchup, connectivity, and compatibility reports. This manual documents the exact local Windows executable and its matching upstream v1.2.6 source, including behaviors that the shorter built-in switch list does not expose.
help:metadata.help:document-status: Verified against the local executable and matching tagged upstream source.

help:semantic-model.help:title: How this XML is connected
help:semantic-model.help:description: The document hierarchy is readable by people; stable identifiers, typed references, prerequisites, constraints, and the relation graph make it usable as a knowledge base. Consumers can resolve every internal *-ref attribute and xref to an xml:id, then traverse dependencies in either direction.

help:topic.help:title: Quick start
help:topic.help:purpose: Calculate a conventional rating list from one PGN file.

help:result.help:description: Ratings are placed on a scale whose pool average is 2300. The default table shows rank, player, rating, points, games, and score percentage. With no simulations, its ERROR column is omitted.

help:caveats.help:item: The file must contain case-sensitive White, Black, and Result tags in Ordo's supported line-oriented form.
The usable result graph must be well connected; inspect failures with the group workflow.
Point ratings are relative. Choose an explicit anchor when comparison with an established scale matters.

help:topic.help:title: Mental model
help:topic.help:summary: Ordo is an in-memory result-pool estimator. It turns decisive and drawn encounters into a connected comparison graph, fits relative strengths under a logistic expectancy model, optionally estimates nuisance parameters and sampling uncertainty, and renders several views of the fitted pool.

help:capabilities.help:capability: Read multiple result-only or full PGN files into one pool.
Apply aliases before inclusion, exclusion, priors, and reports.
Detect independent or directionally underconstrained groups and perfect-score boundary cases.
Use iterative moment matching by default or full maximum likelihood when selected or required by priors.
Replay fitted outcome probabilities to estimate standard errors, pairwise margins, and confidence factors.
Write text, CSV, Elostat-compatible files, matrices, head-to-head, and group reports.

help:non-goals.help:item: Ordo does not parse or validate chess moves; only the White, Black, and Result tag lines matter.
Ordo does not preserve PGN or produce a cleaned PGN; use Ordoprep for that.
Ordo does not make ratings from disconnected pools inherently comparable.
Ordo's simulated error bars describe sampling variability under its fitted model, not every source of real-world uncertainty.

help:topic.help:title: Command syntax and source order

help:syntax-notes.help:note: Use -- before positional paths that begin with a hyphen.
Quote paths containing spaces. This executable has no standard-input switch.
Options may appear around positional inputs, but all input sources are assembled and read in the fixed order below.

help:input-composition.help:source-order: The path supplied by the last -p occurrence, if any.
Paths from the list supplied by the last -P occurrence, in list order.
Positional PGN paths, in command-line order.

help:topic.help:memory-note: Games, encounters, and participant names are accumulated in memory before fitting.

help:topic.help:title: Processing pipeline
help:topic.help:summary: Option timing explains why canonicalization changes filters, why low-output thresholds do not change ratings, and why some report modes exit early.

help:stage.name: options
help:stage.help:description: Parse switches, defaults, conflicts, and column formatting.

help:stage.name: aliases
help:stage.help:description: Load the alias map before any player is created.

help:stage.name: ingest
help:stage.help:description: Read PGN sources and retain completed result triples.

help:stage.name: ignore-draws
help:stage.help:description: If requested, mark drawn games ignored before membership filtering and analysis.

help:stage.name: membership
help:stage.help:description: Apply one include list or one exclude list to canonical names.

help:stage.name: aggregate
help:stage.help:description: Build players and aggregate White/Black encounter counts.

help:stage.name: priors
help:stage.help:description: Resolve hard anchors, loose anchors, pairwise relations, and white/draw settings against the selected pool.

help:stage.name: groups
help:stage.help:description: Check rating connectivity by default, or write the requested group report.

help:stage.name: perfect-boundaries
help:stage.help:description: Temporarily remove unanchored all-win and all-loss boundary players so the ordinary pool can converge.

help:stage.name: fit
help:stage.help:description: Fit ratings and any requested nuisance parameters.

help:stage.name: simulate
help:stage.help:description: When the count exceeds one, replay fitted outcomes and measure rating dispersion.

help:stage.name: restore
help:stage.help:description: Restore original encounters for reporting and assign finite bounds to removed perfect players.

help:stage.name: report
help:stage.help:description: Apply display thresholds and write each requested view.

help:subtopic.help:title: Recognized PGN
help:subtopic.help:description: The scanner recognizes lines beginning exactly and case-sensitively with [White ", [Black ", and [Result ". Conventional one-tag-per-line PGN is safest. Movetext, comments, and all other tags are ignored.
help:subtopic.help:warning: Any other Result value is a fatal input error. A game needs White, Black, and Result tags to become a usable record.

help:subtopic.help:title: Alias CSV
help:subtopic.help:semantics: Every alias in a row maps to its first field. Matching is exact and case-sensitive. Canonicalization happens before filtering, anchoring, priors, and reporting.

help:subtopic.help:title: Include and exclude name lists
help:subtopic.help:format: One CSV field per nonblank line; quoted names are accepted.
help:subtopic.help:warning: The v1.2.6 source requires exactly one CSV field per row. Older prose saying that only the first column is read is too permissive; do not add annotation columns.
help:subtopic.help:selection-rule: An included game requires both canonical player names to be listed.
A game is excluded if either canonical player name is listed.
help:subtopic.help:warning: Names not found in the pool generate warnings unless --no-warnings is active.

help:subtopic.help:title: PGN source list
help:subtopic.help:format: One CSV field containing one path per nonblank line. Paths are opened in list order.

help:subtopic.help:title: Multiple hard anchors
help:subtopic.help:semantics: Fix each named player exactly at the supplied rating. Use exactly two fields for portability; v1.2.6 ignores extras.

help:subtopic.help:title: Loose anchors
Pairwise rating relations
Column-format CSV
help:subtopic.help:semantics: Override a report column's heading and text width. The width must exceed the heading length; rank/name column 0 is auto-sized. Headings also flow into CSV.

help:subtopic.help:title: Logistic expectancy
help:subtopic.help:formula: P(B scores over A) = 1 / (1 + exp(-beta * (R_B - R_A)))
help:subtopic.help:description: Higher ratings mean greater strength. The scale parameter beta is chosen so the rating gap supplied by -z gives 76 percent expectancy.

help:subtopic.help:title: Default estimator
help:subtopic.help:description: The ordinary solver iteratively adjusts player ratings to minimize squared differences between observed points and model-expected points. It is fast and normally agrees closely with full maximum likelihood.

help:subtopic.help:title: Maximum likelihood
help:subtopic.help:description: -M uses the complete win/draw/loss likelihood. Loose player priors, pairwise relations, and uncertain white/draw parameters require this mode and enable it automatically.

help:subtopic.help:title: Draw-aware outcome probabilities
help:subtopic.help:description: Ordo uses the equal-opponent draw rate together with rating difference to divide total expectancy into win, draw, and loss probabilities. In maximum-likelihood fits this affects the game likelihood; in simulations it governs generated W/D/L outcomes.

help:subtopic.help:title: Color advantage
help:subtopic.help:description: A white advantage is a rating offset added to White's expected performance. It may be fixed, constrained by a Gaussian prior, or estimated from the pool.

help:topic.help:title: Reference level, anchors, and scale

help:subtopic.help:title: Ratings need an additive reference
help:subtopic.help:description: Game results identify differences, not an absolute zero. With no anchor, Ordo shifts the fitted list to the average set by -a, 2300 by default. A hard anchor fixes a named participant instead; a loose anchor supplies uncertain outside information.

help:subtopic.help:title: Reference choices
help:subtopic.help:choice: One named hard anchor at the value from -a.
Multiple named hard anchors from a file.
One or more uncertain player priors from a file.
Uncertain pairwise differences from a file.

help:subtopic.help:title: Scale is distinct from reference
help:subtopic.help:description: -z controls how many rating points represent a given expectancy; it does not choose the list's average. The default is 202 points for 76 percent expectancy.

help:topic.help:warning: Ratings from separate pools are not automatically comparable merely because they share an average or scale. Use shared participants or defensible priors and consistent modeling conditions.

help:subtopic.help:title: Connectivity is checked by default
help:subtopic.help:description: Ordo constructs a directed result graph from aggregated pairings. A draw or mixed results supplies a connection in both directions; a one-sided sweep supplies only the winner-to-loser direction. Cycles form strongly connected groups. A conventional finite joint fit requires the retained ordinary pool to be well connected.
help:subtopic.help:group-order: Reported groups are ordered by descending participant count, with alphabetical tie-breaking.

help:subtopic.help:title: All-win and all-loss boundary players
help:subtopic.help:description: Unanchored participants with 100 percent or 0 percent scores have an infinite optimum in an unconstrained logistic fit. Ordo removes them recursively while fitting the ordinary pool, then restores them with finite one-draw bounds for reporting.
help:subtopic.help:marker: A perfect winner's displayed rating is a lower bound.
A perfect loser's displayed rating is an upper bound.
The participant has no retained games.
help:subtopic.help:note: Anchored or priored boundary players may remain finite because outside information constrains them.

help:subtopic.help:title: Forcing a disconnected fit
help:subtopic.help:description: -G bypasses group checking. It does not create missing information: fitting may be slow or fail, and offsets between independent components are arbitrary. Prefer diagnosing and repairing the pool.

help:topic.help:title: Simulation, error margins, and pairwise confidence

help:subtopic.help:title: Monte Carlo method
help:subtopic.help:description: Ordo samples new outcomes from the fitted matchup probabilities, refits each synthetic pool, and measures rating dispersion. Execution occurs only when -s is greater than one. The upstream manual recommends at least about 100 simulations; more than about 1000 is usually unnecessary.

help:subtopic.help:title: What a row error is relative to
help:subtopic.help:description: With one hard anchor, row errors default to changes relative to that anchor, whose displayed error is zero. Without such an anchor they are relative to the simulated pool average. -V selects pool-relative errors even when a single anchor exists.
help:subtopic.help:warning: Do not infer a two-player difference error by mechanically combining two row errors. Use the pairwise error matrix.

help:subtopic.help:title: Confidence level
help:subtopic.help:description: -F converts simulated standard deviations to symmetric normal confidence half-widths. The default 95 percent interval is approximately plus or minus 1.96 standard deviations.

help:subtopic.help:title: Confidence for superiority
help:subtopic.help:description: CFS is the simulated probability, expressed as a percentage, that one player's rating exceeds another's under Ordo's simulation model.

help:output.help:title: Rating text
help:output.help:description: Written to -o when supplied; otherwise the ordinary report goes to standard output. Without simulations the ERROR column is removed.

help:output.help:title: Rating CSV
help:output.help:description: May coexist with text. Column 0 expands to separate rank and PLAYER fields. Without simulations a selected ERROR field contains a hyphen placeholder.

help:output.help:title: Elostat compatibility set
help:output.help:description: Overwrites general.dat, rating.dat, and programs.dat in the current working directory.

help:output.help:title: Head-to-head report
help:output.help:description: Summarizes each pairing; simulation-dependent difference uncertainty and CFS are available when simulations run.

help:output.help:title: Connectivity group report
help:output.help:description: If neither text nor CSV rating output is explicitly requested, Ordo writes this report and exits successfully before rating. If -o or -c is also supplied, it continues into rating and still enforces post-purge connectivity.

help:output.help:title: Pairwise confidence-margin matrix
help:output.help:prerequisite: Requires more than one simulation; otherwise the file is silently not created.

help:output.help:title: CFS matrix
help:output.help:prerequisite: Requires more than one simulation; otherwise the file is silently not created.

help:columns.help:column: Rank and player name; CSV expands this to two fields.
Confidence half-width at the selected confidence level.
Points divided by games, as a percentage.
CFS against the next row in rating order.
Draws divided by games, as a percentage.
Effective opponent count, exp(-sum f_i ln f_i); equals the unique count when games are evenly distributed.

help:subtopic.help:title: Formatting details
help:subtopic.help:description: The verified default for -N is 1,0: one decimal for ratings/errors and zero decimals for text percentages. This differs from stale manual prose. Text points retain one decimal. CSV uses fixed precision for several statistics; its rating, error, and opponent-average fields follow the first -N value, while its points and percentages are not controlled uniformly by the second value.
help:subtopic.help:note: Rows are sorted by descending rating. The output game threshold changes visibility only, not the fitted data.

help:constraints.help:title: Conflicts, dependencies, and semantic rules
help:constraints.help:rule: -m conflicts with an explicitly supplied -a or any -A.
-y conflicts with an explicitly supplied -a, but may coexist with -A.
Include and exclude modes are mutually exclusive.
A group report cannot be combined with forced group-check bypass.

help:constraints.help:rule: All later name matching uses canonicalized identities.
The game threshold filters final rows only and never removes data from the fit.

help:workflow.help:title: Rate one clean connected pool
help:workflow.help:why: Uses the conventional 2300 mean, 202-point scale, zero White advantage, and 50 percent equal-player draw rate.

help:workflow.help:title: Rate several PGN sources as one pool
help:workflow.help:why: Reads baseline first, then each path in seasons.txt, then the positional files.

help:workflow.help:title: Normalize identities and select a closed roster
help:workflow.help:why: Aliases are resolved first; a game remains only when both canonical names appear in roster.csv.
help:workflow.help:see-also: Ordoprep XML help for cleaning, filtering, and splitting PGN before this step.

help:workflow.help:title: Fix one known participant
help:workflow.help:why: Places the entire connected pool relative to Reference Engine = 3200.

help:workflow.help:title: Use several exact reference ratings
help:workflow.help:warning: Exact anchors can conflict statistically; use loose anchors when outside ratings have uncertainty.

help:workflow.help:title: Blend uncertain external ratings with the pool
help:workflow.help:why: Automatically uses maximum likelihood and Gaussian priors.

help:workflow.help:title: Relate engine versions and display only newer ones
help:workflow.help:why: Each relation constrains New minus Old; -R hides the second-listed old version from rating rows.

help:workflow.help:title: Estimate White advantage and draw tendency
help:workflow.help:why: Fits color and draw parameters from the same selected pool and reports them after the rating table.

help:workflow.help:title: Add 95 percent rating margins
help:workflow.help:why: Runs 500 fitted-pool replays using up to four simulation workers.

help:workflow.help:title: Generate pairwise uncertainty and superiority matrices
help:workflow.help:why: The matrix uses pairwise simulated differences, which are more appropriate than combining row errors.

help:workflow.help:title: Create a concise CSV for downstream tooling
help:workflow.help:why: Includes identity, rating, record, opponent count, and diversity; displays players with at least 20 games.

help:workflow.help:title: Diagnose a disconnected pool
help:workflow.help:why: With no explicit -o or -c, writes the group report and exits before rating.
help:workflow.help:next-step: Find missing cross-group games, correct split identities with aliases, select one component, or add defensible external constraints.

help:workflow.help:title: Keep a group audit beside a valid rating report
help:workflow.help:why: Explicit rating output prevents the group-only early exit; the pool must still pass connectivity.

help:workflow.help:title: Inspect the expectancy curve
help:workflow.help:why: Needs no PGN and makes the meaning of the rating scale concrete.

help:workflow.help:title: Produce Elostat-compatible files safely
help:workflow.help:why: Isolates the three fixed output filenames in a dedicated directory.

help:recommendations.help:item: Use -o and/or -c so rating data is not mixed with progress or --timelog text on stdout.
Add -q for routine batch runs, but treat stderr warnings and nonzero status as diagnostic signals.
Write outputs to distinct paths; verify that simulation-dependent files exist only after using -s greater than one.
Version-control alias, selection, anchor, relation, and column-format inputs with the PGN provenance.
Record Ordo version, scale, anchor policy, White/draw settings, estimator, filters, and simulation count alongside published ratings.
Use CSV for parsing; formatted text widths and headings are designed for people.

help:reproducibility-record.help:field: All auxiliary file contents and hashes
Complete command line and working directory

help:problem.help:cause: No -p, -P, or positional PGN source resolved.
help:problem.help:resolution: Supply at least one PGN file, unless using an informational option or -T.

help:problem.symptom: Fatal error around a Result tag
help:problem.help:cause: The Result value is not one of 1-0, 0-1, 1/2-1/2, =-=, or *.
help:problem.help:resolution: Normalize the PGN result tag; use * only for games meant to be discarded.

help:problem.symptom: Expected games or players are absent
help:problem.help:cause: Tags may differ in case/layout, the game may lack a complete triple, Result may be *, or include/exclude rules may remove it.
help:problem.help:resolution: Inspect exact tag lines and canonical names; preprocess unusual PGN with Ordoprep.

help:problem.symptom: Selection file reports a malformed row
help:problem.help:cause: Include/exclude files require exactly one CSV field per nonblank line.
help:problem.help:resolution: Remove comments and annotation columns; quote a name only when CSV quoting is needed.

help:problem.symptom: Anchor, prior, or relation player is not found
help:problem.help:cause: The exact case-sensitive canonical name is absent after PGN selection, often because of an alias or filter mismatch.
help:problem.help:resolution: Check alias output identity and ensure the player retains at least one selected record where required.

help:problem.help:cause: Results contain independent components or a one-way result structure that cannot determine finite relative offsets.
help:problem.help:resolution: Run -g without -o/-c, inspect groups, correct identities or inputs, and add genuine cross-group evidence. Use -G only with full understanding.

help:problem.symptom: Rating has a greater-than or less-than marker
help:problem.help:cause: The participant won every retained game or lost every retained game without a finite external constraint.
help:problem.help:resolution: Interpret the value as a lower or upper bound, add more varied results, or supply a defensible prior.

help:problem.help:cause: No simulations ran; -s 0 and -s 1 both disable simulated uncertainty.
help:problem.help:resolution: Use -s 100 or more for a stable estimate.

help:problem.symptom: Requested error or CFS matrix was not created
help:problem.help:cause: Ordo silently skips these files unless the simulation count exceeds one.
help:problem.help:resolution: Add a practical -s value such as 500 and check the output path again.

help:problem.symptom: Pairwise significance inferred from row errors seems inconsistent
help:problem.help:cause: Row errors share an anchor or pool reference and are correlated.
help:problem.help:resolution: Use -e for pairwise difference margins or -C for simulated superiority probabilities.
Use include/exclude inputs to change fitted data; use -t only for presentation.

help:problem.help:cause: Group mode exits after its report unless -o or -c is explicitly supplied.
help:problem.help:resolution: Add -o ratings.txt or -c ratings.csv if the pool is connected and both outputs are wanted.

help:problem.help:cause: --timelog writes checkpoints to stdout independently of quiet mode.
help:problem.help:resolution: Route ratings with -o and reserve stdout for timing diagnostics.

help:problem.help:cause: -m cannot be combined with explicit -a or -A; -y cannot be combined with explicit -a.
help:problem.help:resolution: Choose one coherent reference policy and remove the conflicting switch.

help:problem.help:cause: Automatic estimation cannot coexist with fixed/prior forms for the same parameter.
help:problem.help:resolution: Choose -W or -w/-u, and independently choose -D or -d/-k.

help:problem.symptom: Forced fit is slow, unstable, or implausible
help:problem.help:cause: -G bypassed an identifiability check without adding information.
help:problem.help:resolution: Stop forcing, inspect -g output, and repair or constrain the comparison graph.

help:problem.help:cause: -E always targets general.dat, rating.dat, and programs.dat in the current directory.
help:problem.help:resolution: Run in a dedicated output directory and preserve prior artifacts before rerunning.

help:problem.symptom: Default decimals differ from the old manual
help:problem.help:cause: The verified v1.2.6 executable defaults to -N 1,0, while stale prose describes 0,1.

help:term.help:name: anchor
help:term.help:definition: External information that fixes or constrains the additive rating reference.

help:term.help:name: canonical name
help:term.help:definition: The first field of an alias row and the identity used after synonym replacement.

help:term.help:name: CFS
help:term.help:definition: Confidence for superiority: simulated probability that one fitted rating exceeds another.

help:term.help:name: well connected
help:term.help:definition: A result graph whose directional evidence jointly identifies finite relative strengths for the ordinary pool.

help:term.help:name: Elo-like rating
help:term.help:definition: A scalar strength coordinate whose differences map through a logistic expectancy curve.

help:term.help:name: estimand
help:term.help:definition: The quantity a particular selected dataset and statistical model are intended to estimate.

help:term.help:name: hard anchor
help:term.help:definition: A player rating fixed exactly, with no estimated uncertainty.

help:term.help:name: loose anchor
help:term.help:definition: A Gaussian prior centered on an external rating with a stated standard deviation.

help:term.help:name: maximum likelihood
help:term.help:definition: Parameter values that maximize the probability of the observed W/D/L outcomes and any Gaussian priors.

help:term.help:name: opponent diversity
help:term.help:definition: The exponential Shannon entropy of opponent game shares, interpreted as an effective opponent count.

help:term.help:name: perfect player
help:term.help:definition: An unanchored participant with only wins or only losses in the retained result pool.

help:term.help:name: prior
help:term.help:definition: External probabilistic information added to the game likelihood.

help:term.help:name: scale
help:term.help:definition: The conversion between rating difference and expected score; distinct from the list's additive reference.

help:term.help:name: simulated rating error
help:term.help:definition: Rating dispersion under repeated synthetic result pools drawn from Ordo's fitted model.

help:term.help:name: Ordo
help:term.help:definition: The rating and reporting program documented here.

help:term.help:name: Ordoprep
help:term.help:definition: A companion program for compacting, selecting, filtering, and partitioning PGN results before rating.
